name: René Descartes
summary: René Descartes, the French philosopher of methodical doubt, held that a private person should not try to reform a state by overturning it, resolved to obey his country's laws and customs and religion while rebuilding his own opinions, and treated reason as the one faculty shared equally by all humans and absent in animals, which he saw as machines.

sources.title: Discourse on the Method of Rightly Conducting One's Reason and of Seeking Truth in the Sciences (1637; Veitch translation), Project Gutenberg
sources.author: René Descartes
sources.usedFor: Part II (reforming a state, restless meddlers, gradual smoothing of paths), Part III (provisional morals: obey the laws and customs of one's country), Part V (reason as universal instrument, machines and brutes).
sources.library: 59 Descartes - Discourse on the Method of Rightly Conducting One's Reason a.txt

sources.title: René Descartes, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.author: Gary Hatfield
